claims.text: The governing distance is the trace, not the rounded trip record: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 23.97 km against a booked optimal of 18.0 km, an excess of 5.97 km — 33.17% of optimal. Both limbs of POL-RD-01 pass on that figure (33.17% > 20%, and 5.97 km > 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. The rider's '6 km' is his own estimate; the measured excess is 5.97 km and the claim is made at that figure, which is the field POL-RD-01 makes governing where the trace and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) and has discharged it: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry TRP-00114, and limb (b) is met by the 5.97 km excess measured from an unimpaired trace. The burden therefore shifts to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause to invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12. His counterparty statement points to none, and POL-RD-08 provides that a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge that burden.

The detour was the driver's choice, not the rider's instruction. The only relevant chat traffic is the rider asking at 18:58:40 'adam road?? jurong is the other way' — a query sent 18 minutes into the trip, and the driver replying 'AYE jam boss, this way faster'. Nothing in the chat_log asks for a detour, and waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so there is no waypoint to test against the 200 m radius and no road is named for the rider. POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record and no distance is excluded under it.

The driver's explanation is an external-traffic assertion and the bundle contains no traffic_advisory to test it against. EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — I disclose that impairment, and I cite it for no fact other than its own absence. Under POL-RD-13 the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion 'AYE was crawling from the Alexandra exit' carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The deviation therefore stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route, with no amended optimal supplied by the driver or derivable from the record.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 against the booked optimal route: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 30) x 1.6) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 of on-optimal-route ERP = 44.42. Charged_total was 58.10, so the refund is 58.10 - 44.42 = 13.68 before rounding, payable as 13.70 rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05. That is 23.5% of the charge, above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and far below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. The 1.6 multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and is applied to the recomputed fare as the rider accepts it; the refund does not claw back the surge, only the distance and time actually driven off the optimal route.

On the ERP lines, only the Kim Keat Link gantry (SGD 2.50) lies on the optimal route and it is already inside the recomputed fare. The Adam Road gantry (SGD 2.00) is billed as off_optimal_route and is charged to a corridor the optimal route does not use; under POL-RD-09(1) that charge is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund and must never be added on top of it. The total refund is therefore SGD 13.70, not SGD 15.70, and I itemise the SGD 2.00 here for transparency only.

Nothing on this record supports holding the money instead of paying it. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 241 fixes, 100% coverage, a 10 s sample interval against a 10 s expected interval, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0, so POL-RD-10(3) cannot fire. Because the driver cited no advisory identifier at all, POL-RD-13(1) keeps the absent advisory out of POL-RD-10(5) — an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one. Both billed gantries match the trace within the 250 m radius (nearest fixes at 0.0 m and 8.76 m), so there is no phantom line and POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged. The money should move, and it should move now.

That distinction controls the remedy: this is a non-material deviation, so POL-RD-06's FULL_REFUND uplift and its conduct referral are not engaged and the case remains on the POL-RD-02 arithmetic track.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. POL-RD-02 gives recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.6) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 on-optimal-route ERP = 44.42. Charged_total is 58.10, so the refund is 58.10 - 44.42 = 13.68, rounded up to 13.70 on separate lines. That is below the 15.00 the rider contends for, and at 23.5% of the charge it is nowhere near the 90% threshold that would convert this into a FULL_REFUND.

The rider expressly accepts the 1.6 surge, and the multiplier is recorded on the fare_breakdown (not on the trip_record, which carries no such field). The recomputed fare must therefore carry the surge on base, distance and time; the refund cannot be enlarged by reading the surge as absent.

Of the 4.50 of ERP, only the 2.50 Kim Keat Link gantry lies on the optimal route - the trace passes within 0 m of it - and is properly chargeable; the 2.00 Adam Road gantry is the sole off-route line. Under POL-RD-09(1) both are already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 recomputation (which credits only on-optimal-route gantries), so neither may ever be added on top of the 13.70 as a second payment.

The bundle's traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00114-01, is MISSING and carries weight 0.0, and the driver's congestion explanation in the chat names no advisory identifier. Under POL-RD-13(1) a party asserting an external traffic cause who cites no advisory artifact cannot be invoking an exculpatory clause against a cited artifact, so the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction; the matter resolves on the arithmetic evidence and does not escalate.

On the driver's side, even if POL-RD-06 were consulted, the permitted fields show 1 deviation flag over 412 completed trips (EV-DPROF-00114), far below the 3-flag or 0.05-ratio pattern test, so no pattern exists. No exoneration applies. POL-RD-03 needs a traffic advisory and none exists: EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, and under POL-RD-13 the driver's congestion explanation ('AYE was crawling from the Alexandra exit'), which names no advisory identifier, carries no weight; the deviation stands at the measured figure against the booked optimal route. POL-RD-04 fails because the chat log (EV-CHAT-00114) records a rider query ('adam road?? jurong is the other way') and not a rider instruction, and both messages carry a null waypoint_hint; POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 and POL-RD-12 do not apply on this trip record. The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 on the METERED fare model: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.6, the surge read from EV-FARE-00114) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 of on-optimal-route ERP = 44.42. Charged total 58.10 less 44.42 = 13.68, rounded up to 13.70. That is above the 0.50 de-minimis floor and 23.5% of the charge, well below the 90% full-refund share, so this is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.70 - not the 15.00 contended and not a full refund. The SGD 2.00 Adam Road gantry (EV-FARE-00114) is the only off-route ERP line and is already comprehended inside the recomputation, so it is itemised for transparency but never added on top; the SGD 2.50 Kim Keat Link gantry lies on the optimal route and is properly chargeable. Because the SGD 13.70 exceeds the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, the amount is issued but held for release under POL-GEN-05. ruling.explanation:
Both sides agree on the arithmetic, and so do I. The measured route is 23.97 km (gps_trace.trace_distance_km, the governing field under POL-RD-01 where it disagrees with the rounded trip record) against a booked optimal of 18.0 km: an excess of 5.97 km, 33.17%. That clears POL-RD-01's establishment gate (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so a deviation is ESTABLISHED. It does not clear the materiality gate (over 50% or over 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06's FULL_REFUND uplift and its driver-conduct referral are not engaged, and no POL-RD-06 pattern exists anyway: the driver's trailing-90-day figure is 1 flag over 412 completed trips, below both limbs of the test. The rider's '6 km' is his own estimate; the claim is met at the measured 5.97 km.

The driver's explanation - AYE crawling from the Alexandra exit, so he went up and over on the PIE - is an external-traffic assertion. The bundle holds no traffic advisory covering this trip: EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), and the driver cited no advisory identifier. Under POL-RD-13(1) the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction, so this does not escalate; under POL-RD-08 the uncited traffic assertion does not discharge the driver's shifted burden, and POL-RD-03 is unavailable. The rider gave no detour instruction: the only chat traffic is his 18:58:40 query ('adam road?? jurong is the other way') and the driver's reply, both with waypoint_hint null and no road requested by the rider, so POL-RD-04 excludes no distance. POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 and POL-RD-12 do not apply: no endpoint was amended, the fare model is METERED (not UPFRONT_QUOTE), and the vehicle is RYDE_X (not RYDE_POOL). The trace is unbroken - 241 fixes, 100% coverage, a 10 s interval against a 10 s expected interval, no gaps, max gap 0 - so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and no POL-RD-10 trigger fires.

Recomputed under POL-RD-02: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.6) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 of on-optimal-route ERP = 44.42. The 1.6 multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, as the rider accepts. Charged_total was 58.10, so the refund is 58.10 - 44.42 = 13.68 before rounding, payable as SGD 13.70 rounded up to the nearest 0.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and 23.5% of the charge, far below the 90% share that would make it a FULL_REFUND, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

On the ERP lines: only the Kim Keat Link gantry (2.50) lies on the optimal route and is already inside the recomputed fare. The Adam Road gantry (2.00) is off-optimal-route, and under POL-RD-09(1) it is already comprehended in the 13.70 and must never be added on top - the total is 13.70, not 15.70. Both gantries match the trace well within the 250 m radius (nearest fixes at 0.0 m and 8.76 m), so there is no phantom line and POL-RD-09(4) produces no billing-integrity referral. No clause produces a referral in this case, so the referrals list is empty, and the money moves now. This figure (13.70) exceeds the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so it is issued but held for release under POL-GEN-05.
